customer_john: Hey team — since last night our private inference endpoint intermittently fails. Some requests get TLS handshake timeouts, others 502 empty responses. Happening from our app servers in us-west-2 VPC. Ticket #INC-12345.

support_sam: Sorry you're hitting this, John. Can you paste a minimal curl/openssl snippet and pi/trace so we can see the failure mode? Also which subnet/NAT are you using?

customer_john: Curl output: `curl -v https://inference.private.redwood.ai -o /dev/null` shows:
* Connected to inference.private.redwood.ai (10.10.10.7) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: read timeout
* Failed to receive HTTP response: Empty reply from server
OpenSSL: `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.10.7:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.ai` hangs and then: `read:errno=104`
We route egress via a NAT gateway (nat-0a1b2c3d) that sits in a public subnet; NACLs were recently tightened last week.

alex_netops: Thanks. Two quick things to check: 1) NACLs are stateless — you must allow return ephemeral ports on BOTH directions. 2) NAT source port translation uses high ephemeral ports on the NAT — if NACL denies that range it will drop the return TCP segments.
Can you run on an affected app host: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and host 10.10.10.7 and port 443' -w /tmp/cap.pcap` and also `sudo ss -tanp | grep 443` and share the first few lines of tcpdump (text) if possible.

customer_john: Pasted tcpdump output snippet:
```
12:34:10.123456 IP 10.10.10.7.443 > 172.31.20.45.54823: Flags [R.], seq 1001, ack 2001, win 0, length 0
12:34:10.123457 IP 172.31.20.45.54823 > 10.10.10.7.443: Flags [S], seq 2001, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
```
So the server (10.10.10.7) is sending RST back to the ephemeral port on our app host.

maria_oncall: That RST pattern usually means the return packet got altered/dropped mid-path or NACL blocked the NAT-mapped source port and the server closed the connection. Check the NACL on the public subnet where the NAT lives — look for deny rules covering 32768-65535 (or your configured ephemeral range). If NACL denies outbound/ inbound for those ports the NAT translation won't be able to complete.
NACLs are evaluated per direction; with a stateless NACL you need explicit inbound AND outbound allow entries for the port range used by the translation.

alex_netops: Another angle — corporate inline TLS inspection appliances sometimes rewrite SNI or terminate and re-initiate TLS with different source port behaviour; that can also cause server RSTs if the backend expects original IP:port mapping. But given the recent NACL hardening note, start there.

support_sam: Quick repro steps you can run to validate before/after: 
1) `traceroute -T -p 443 inference.private.redwood.ai`
2) `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.10.7:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.ai -tlsextdebug -state`
3) `curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://inference.private.redwood.ai`
If the failure goes away after editing NACL, it's the port-range deny.

customer_john: We checked the NACL on the NAT public subnet — there was a deny rule for 61000-65535 that we added last week (priority 100). I added a temporary allow entry for 32768-65535 inbound and outbound and tested. After the change the same curl/openSSL commands now succeed (handshake completes).

support_sam: Great — that matches the diagnosis. For a permanent fix: either widen the allowed ephemeral range on the NACL to cover the NAT port allocation range, or move the NAT behind a subnet with more permissive NACLs. Also verify any downstream firewall/appliance doesn't have asymmetric rules.

maria_oncall: Notes to include in the ticket: 
- Cause: NACL deny on high ephemeral port range causing asymmetric drop of NAT return traffic -> TLS handshake failures / empty replies.
- Fix: Add allow rules for ephemeral port range (recommend 32768-65535 or check OS NAT config if using custom range).
- Mitigation: Use stateful security groups for simpler egress, or put NAT in a subnet with conservative NACLs.

customer_john: Confirming everything stable for ~30 minutes. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup: Ticket INC-12345 updated with remediation steps.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: infra-change/nacl-update@main (PR #678) — rolled out to us-west-2 NAT subnet.

support_sam: Closing loop — I'll mark the incident resolved and add the recommended NACL checklist to our KB (private-vpc/networking/ephemeral-port-guidance). If anything flares up ping me.

customer_john: Thanks all!
